topic: Why a first Claude skill fails, and the fix for each cause
audience: Professionals who tried making a Claude skill and gave up, or are about to make their first
goal: Get a first skill working by checking the seven common failure points, using the free guides on mojeedabisiga.com/learn
notes: From the issue Make your first skill: zip the folder, not the files inside it. The zip must contain weekly-report/SKILL.md. On a Mac: right-click the folder, Compress. On Windows: right-click the folder, Send to → Compressed (zipped) folder. Upload the zip as it is; don't unzip it. This is where most first uploads fail.
Turn skills on: Settings → Capabilities → Create and edit files (older layout: Code execution and file creation). Team plans: on by default; Enterprise: an owner turns them on first.
Upload: Customize → Skills → + → Create skill → Upload a skill. Check the skill's switch is on. Claude ignored your skill? Check the switch first: it's off more often than you'd think.
Name rules: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only; 64 characters at most; same as the folder's name; can't contain 'claude' or 'anthropic'.

Description: Claude decides when to use a skill from the description alone. Say what it does and when to use it, third person, 200 characters at most in the Claude apps, no tags in angle brackets. Weak: 'Helps with reports.' Strong: 'Turns the week's notes and numbers into our team's weekly report format. Use when someone asks for the weekly report or pastes weekly updates.'
One skill, one job. A job that is really three jobs: split it, or the skill does all three badly. A job you do once a quarter: you won't remember to use it.
Test with five requests: three that should use the skill, two that shouldn't. This is the step everyone skips.
Fix order when Claude doesn't use it: 1) check the switch, 2) name it in your request ('Use my weekly-report skill on these notes.'), 3) rewrite the description; then run the five requests again.
Instructions: under 500 lines; numbered steps, mistakes to avoid, one short real example. Never put passwords, API keys or personal data in a skill.
Mojeed's free guides are at https://mojeedabisiga.com/learn (the pages are listed in learn_catalog.json).
